cues.en: Breakfast of champions. What's the difference between eating less food and eating no food? Well, let's look at two different situations.
cues.zh: 王者之餐。吃得少和不吃有什么区别？我们来看看两种不同的情况。

cues.en: a study called the Minnesota Starvation Experiment was conducted and was designed to understand the effects of caloric restriction on the body in order to gain some knowledge that would help people starving in the aftermath of world war two.
cues.zh: 一项名为明尼苏达饥饿实验的研究展开了，旨在了解限制热量对身体的影响，从而获取能帮助二战后饥饿人群的知识。

cues.en: 36 healthy men with an average height of one hundred seventy eight centimeters, about five foot ten, and an average weight of sixty nine point three kilograms or one hundred and fifty three pounds were selected.
cues.zh: 36名健康的男性被选中，他们平均身高178厘米（约5英尺10英寸），平均体重69.3公斤（约153磅）。

cues.en: For three months, they ate a diet of 3,200 calories per day. Then, for six months, they ate only 1,570
cues.zh: 在三个月里，他们每天摄入3200卡路里的饮食。接着在六个月里，他们每天只吃1570

cues.en: calories.
cues.zh: 卡路里。

cues.en: However, caloric intake was adjusted to attempt to have the men lose 1.1 kilograms per week meaning some men got less than 1,000 calories per day. The foods given were high in carbohydrates, things like potatoes, turnips, bread and macaroni.
cues.zh: 然而，热量摄入会根据情况调整，以使受试者每周减重1.1公斤，这意味着有些人每天摄入的热量不到1000卡路里。提供的食物富含碳水化合物，比如土豆、萝卜、面包和通心粉。

cues.en: Meat and dairy products were rarely given.
cues.zh: 肉类和乳制品极少提供。

cues.en: During the six months, the men experienced profound physical and psychological changes.
cues.zh: 在这六个月期间，这些男性的身体和心理都经历了重大的变化。

cues.en: Everyone complained that they were too cold.
cues.zh: 每个人都抱怨太冷了。

cues.en: One subject talked about having to wear a sweater in July on a sunny day. The subject's body temperatures dropped to an average of 95.8
cues.zh: 有一个受试者谈到在七月的一个晴天还得穿毛衣。受试者的体温平均降到了95.8

cues.en: degrees fahrenheit. Physical endurance dropped by half and strength showed a 21% decrease.
cues.zh: 华氏度。身体耐力下降了一半，力量下降了21%。

cues.en: The men experienced a complete lack of interest in everything except for food,
cues.zh: 这些男人们对除了食物之外的一切事物都完全失去了兴趣，

cues.en: which they were obsessed with. They were plagued with constant and intense hunger.
cues.zh: 他们满脑子只有吃，饱受持续而剧烈的饥饿折磨。

cues.en: There were several cases of neurotic behavior like hoarding cookbooks and utensils.
cues.zh: 还出现了诸如囤积食谱和餐具等好几种神经质行为。

cues.en: Two participants had to be cut from the experiment because they admitted to stealing and eating several raw turnips
cues.zh: 有两名参与者不得不被中途除名，因为他们承认自己偷吃并生吃了好几个萝卜，

cues.en: and taking scraps of food from garbage cans.
cues.zh: 还从垃圾桶里捡食物残渣。

cues.en: At first, the participants were allowed to chew gum until some of the men began chewing up to 40 packages a day.
cues.zh: 起初，参与者们被允许嚼口香糖，直到其中一些人开始一天嚼多达 40 包。

cues.en: Now, compare all this to the case of Angus Barbieri,
cues.zh: 现在，把这一切和 Angus Barbieri 的情况作个对比，

cues.en: a Scottish man who in 1965
cues.zh: 他是 1965 年的一位苏格兰男子，

cues.en: fasted for over three hundred eighty days straight,
cues.zh: 连续绝食了三百八十多天，

cues.en: That is, he took in no food whatsoever,
cues.zh: 也就是说，他没有摄入任何食物，

cues.en: nothing but water, black coffee and straight tea for just over a year. He lost £276
cues.zh: 在短短一年多的时间里，除了水、黑咖啡和纯茶，什么都不吃。他减掉了 276 英镑，

cues.en: going from four hundred fifty six pounds to one hundred eighty. A case report published by the Dundee University Of Department Of Medicine in 1973
cues.zh: 体重从 456 英镑降到了 180 英镑。邓迪大学医学系于 1973 年发表的一份病例报告

cues.en: said:
cues.zh: 指出：

cues.en: The patient remained symptom free, felt well and walked about normally.
cues.zh: 该患者没有出现任何症状，感觉良好，行动正常。

cues.en: And, prolonged fasting in this patient had no ill effects.
cues.zh: 而且，这位患者长时间禁食没有产生任何不良影响。

cues.en: There were no complaints of mind numbing hunger and he kept the weight off. For several years, his weight stayed around one hundred and ninety six pounds.
cues.zh: 没有出现让人头脑发麻的饥饿抱怨，而且他成功保持了减下来的体重。好几年里，他的体重一直维持在 196 英镑左右。

cues.en: This, of course, is not a perfect comparison. With the case of Angus, there's only one subject and his starting weight was drastically higher compared to those in the Minnesota experiment.
cues.zh: 当然，这并不是一个完美的对比。在 Angus 的例子中，只有一个受试者，而且与明尼苏达实验的参与者相比，他的初始体重高得多。

cues.en: However, it does illustrate some very interesting points about just how different of a physiological
cues.zh: 不过，这确实揭示了一些非常有意思的要点，即禁食（也就是彻底不吃东西）

cues.en: response you can get from fasting, that is eating nothing,
cues.zh: 所能带来的生理反应，

cues.en: compared to eating less or caloric restriction.
cues.zh: 相比于少吃或限制热量摄入，究竟有多大差别。

cues.en: Doctor Jason Fung, a Toronto physician specializing in kidney disease and author of the obesity code, says that compared to fasting, caloric reduction will result in less weight loss, more lean mass loss, I e more muscle loss, and more hunger.
cues.zh: Jason Fung 医生是多伦多的一位肾病专家，也是 The Obesity Code 的作者，他指出：相比禁食，减少热量摄入会导致体重减得更少、瘦体重流失更多（即肌肉流失更多），而且饥饿感更强烈。

cues.en: Let's start by talking about hunger.
cues.zh: 我们先从饥饿感聊起。

cues.en: In Upton Sinclair's 1911 book The Fasting Cure, he writes about fasting as a means to improve health. In describing his first couple attempts at fasting, he writes, I was very hungry for the first day, the unwholesome ravening sort of hunger that all dyspeptics know. I had a little hunger the second morning and thereafter, to my great astonishment, no hunger whatever.
cues.zh: 在 Upton Sinclair 1911 年的著作 The Fasting Cure 中，他将禁食视为改善健康的一种手段。在描述自己最初几次尝试禁食时，他写道：“第一天我非常饿，就是所有消化不良患者都深知的那种病态又贪婪的饥饿感。第二天早上还有一点饿，但从那之后，令我大为震惊的是，竟然完全感觉不到饿了。

cues.en: No more interest in food than if I had ever known the taste of it.
cues.zh: 对食物毫无兴趣，就好像我根本不知道食物是什么味道一样。”

cues.en: Sinclair recommends to do quite long fasts, around twelve days or so. In a section addressing concerns about fasting, he writes: Several people have asked me if it would not be better for them to eat very lightly instead of fasting or to content themselves with fasts of two or three days at frequent intervals.
cues.zh: Sinclair 建议进行较长时间的禁食，大约十二天左右。在解答关于禁食疑虑的章节中，他写道：“有好几个人问我，吃得非常清淡来代替禁食，或者频繁进行两三天的短期禁食，会不会更好？

cues.en: My reply to that is I find it very much harder to do that because all the trouble in the fast occurs during the first two or three days.
cues.zh: 我的回答是，我觉得那样做反而要艰难得多，因为禁食中最难受的反应全都发生在头两三天。”

cues.en: It is during those days that you are hungry.
cues.zh: 正是在那些日子里，你会感到饥饿。

cues.en: Then he says, perhaps it might be a good thing to eat very lightly of fruit instead of taking an absolute fast. The only trouble is that I cannot do it. Again and again, I have tried but always with the same result. The light meals are just enough to keep me ravenously hungry.
cues.zh: 接着他说，或许少吃点水果，而不是彻底禁食，会是个好主意。唯一的问题是我做不到。我一次又一次地尝试，结果却总是老样子。清淡的饮食只会让我饿得发慌。

cues.en: In the book, he says you will know when you should finish fasting because your hunger will return.
cues.zh: 他在书中提到，当你的饥饿感回归时，你就知道该结束禁食了。

cues.en: He quotes a letter he received from a 72 year old man saying, after fasting twenty eight days, I began to be hungry and broke my fast with a little grape juice, followed the next day with tomatoes and later with vegetable soup.
cues.zh: 他引用了一位 72 岁老人的来信，信中说：“禁食二十八天后，我开始感到饥饿，于是喝了一点葡萄汁来结束禁食，第二天吃了西红柿，后来又喝了蔬菜汤。”

cues.en: He quotes several other letters he received from his readers and this disappearance and reappearance of hunger is a common theme.
cues.zh: 他还引用了读者发来的几封信，这种饥饿感的消失与再现是一个共同的主题。

cues.en: Everyone who wrote to him fasted for at least ten days, saying they only broke the fast when hunger returned.
cues.zh: 所有写信给他的人都禁食了至少十天，并表示只有在饥饿感回归时才会结束禁食。

cues.en: This phenomenon runs contrary to the idea that one would get hungrier and hungrier as long as they don't eat.
cues.zh: 这种现象与“只要不吃就会越来越饿”的观点相悖。

cues.en: However, most people have experienced for themselves that this is not the case. Some will find that they are not hungry at all in the morning or at least they are not as hungry as they are for lunch or dinner.
cues.zh: 然而，大多数人自身都经历过并非如此的情况。有些人会发现他们早上一点都不饿，或者至少没有午餐或晚餐时那么饿。

cues.en: But unless you are eating in your sleep, the morning is when you have gone the longest without food.
cues.zh: 但除非你在睡梦中进食，否则早上其实是你禁食时间最长的时候。

cues.en: Some Some of this can be explained by the hormone ghrelin.
cues.zh: 其中一些可以用饥饿素这种激素来解释。

cues.en: Ghrelin, known as the hunger hormone,
cues.zh: 饥饿素被称为饥饿激素，

cues.en: has been found to increase appetite and weight gain. A study at the Medical University of Vienna looked at patients participating in a thirty three hour fast.
cues.zh: 已被发现会增加食欲和体重。维也纳医科大学的一项研究观察了参与33小时禁食的患者。

cues.en: Their ghrelin levels were checked every twenty minutes. Here's how the levels changed over time.
cues.zh: 他们的饥饿素水平每20分钟检测一次。下面是这些水平随时间变化的情况。

cues.en: What's interesting is ghrelin is lowest at 9AM
cues.zh: 有趣的是，饥饿素在上午9点最低，

cues.en: which is when they have gone the longest without eating.
cues.zh: 而这正是他们最长时间没吃东西的时候。

cues.en: And ghrelin comes in waves and overall doesn't rise during the period the subjects were fasting.
cues.zh: 饥饿素呈波浪式波动，而且在受试者禁食期间总体上并没有上升。

cues.en: Then, as you can see, ghrelin rises in sync with normal lunch and dinner times as if the body had learned to expect food at that time.
cues.zh: 然后，如你所见，饥饿素会在正常的午餐和晚餐时间同步上升，就好像身体已经学会了在那个时间期待食物。

cues.en: However, that ghrelin rise spontaneously decreases
cues.zh: 然而，这种饥饿素上升会自发下降，

cues.en: after two hours without food.
cues.zh: 在两个小时没有进食之后。

cues.en: I've experienced this kind of spontaneous decrease in hunger myself many times when I was working as a consultant.
cues.zh: 我自己在做顾问时多次经历过这种饥饿感的自发下降。

cues.en: Lunchtime would come and I would be hungry, but I was too busy to eat so I just kept working.
cues.zh: 午餐时间到了，我会饿，但我太忙了没法吃，所以就继续工作。

cues.en: Pretty quickly, I forgot about eating and wasn't particularly hungry until dinner time.
cues.zh: 很快，我就忘了吃这件事，直到晚餐时间都不是特别饿。

cues.en: This is very helpful to keep in mind if you are doing a long fast or even if you're starting intermittent fasting.
cues.zh: 如果你在进行长时间禁食，甚至只是开始间歇性禁食，记住这一点非常有帮助。

cues.en: You're going to get annoying waves of hunger especially around the times you usually eat,
cues.zh: 你会经历一阵阵烦人的饥饿感，尤其是在你通常进食的时间前后，

cues.en: but it won't get worse. The hunger will simply go away if you are patient.
cues.zh: 但它不会变得更糟。只要你耐心一点，饥饿感就会自行消失。

cues.en: Another study concerning ghrelin was done at Aarhus University Hospital in Denmark and it shows what happens if you do a longer fast.
cues.zh: 丹麦奥胡斯大学医院开展了另一项关于胃饥饿素的研究，结果显示了长时间禁食会发生什么。

cues.en: They looked at the ghrelin levels of 33 subjects who fasted for eighty four hours.
cues.zh: 他们观察了 33 名禁食 84 小时受试者的胃饥饿素水平。

cues.en: So did they get increasingly hungrier throughout the fasting period? Well, no. The ghrelin followed similar rhythms each day, but it actually decreased
cues.zh: 那么，在整个禁食期间，他们是不是越来越饿了？其实不是。胃饥饿素每天呈现出相似的节律，但它实际上有所下降

cues.en: the longer they fasted.
cues.zh: 而且禁食时间越长，下降得越多。

cues.en: Going longer without food actually made them less hungry.
cues.zh: 长时间不进食反而会让人没那么饿。

cues.en: This gives credence to what Upton Sinclair and his readers said about hunger disappearing after the first three days of fasting.
cues.zh: 这印证了 Upton Sinclair 及其读者所说的：禁食头三天后，饥饿感会消失。

cues.en: I've done a couple five and six day fasts in the past myself and this indeed was the case. Actually, I did four day fasts last week and again, the fourth day was when I had the least hunger.
cues.zh: 过去我自己也试过几次五天和六天的禁食，确实就是这样。上周我还进行了几次四天禁食，同样是在第四天最不觉得饿。

cues.en: Another thing that may be contributing to this phenomenon is that you are entering ketosis.
cues.zh: 导致这一现象的另一个因素，可能是你进入了酮症状态。

cues.en: Ketosis is a physiological state where your metabolism switches to using primarily fat for energy.
cues.zh: 酮症是一种生理状态，此时你的代谢会转而主要利用脂肪供能。

cues.en: For this reason, ketosis is popular as a weight loss method, but it has many other benefits including better physical and mental efficiency.
cues.zh: 因此，酮症作为一种减重方法很受欢迎，但它还有许多其他益处，包括提高身体和精神效率。

cues.en: Ketosis occurs when you restrict carbohydrates down to 50 grams or less and you don't eat too much protein.
cues.zh: 当你把碳水化合物限制在每天 50 克或更少，并且不摄入过多蛋白质时，就会进入酮症。

cues.en: Everyone's body is a bit different so you might have to eat even less carbohydrate or may have room for more, but the recommended ratio of a ketogenic diet is to get 5% of your calories from carbs, 25% from protein and 75%
cues.zh: 每个人的身体都有些不同，所以你可能需要摄入更少的碳水化合物，也可能可以多摄入一些；但生酮饮食的推荐比例是：5% 的热量来自碳水化合物，25% 来自蛋白质，75%

cues.en: from good fat.
cues.zh: 来自优质脂肪。

cues.en: A simpler way to enter ketosis is just don't eat anything for a long enough time.
cues.zh: 进入生酮状态更简单的方法，就是足够长的时间什么都别吃。

cues.en: This is one of the major points in the difference between fasting and caloric restriction.
cues.zh: 这是断食和热量限制之间最主要的区别之一。

cues.en: The problem with the subjects in the Minnesota Starvation Experiment was that they were eating just enough to keep them out of ketosis and keep their metabolism primed for burning carbohydrate so
cues.zh: 明尼苏达饥饿实验中受试者的问题在于，他们吃得刚好够维持不进入生酮状态，并让新陈代谢保持在燃烧碳水化合物的状态，所以

cues.en: they couldn't use their body fat for energy.
cues.zh: 他们无法利用体内的脂肪来获取能量。

cues.en: This explains a lot of things like why they were losing their strength and why they were very sluggish and cold.
cues.zh: 这就解释了很多现象，比如他们为什么会失去力气，为什么会感到非常迟钝和寒冷。

cues.en: It also clears up why Upton Sinclair said fruit or light meals were just enough to keep him ravenously hungry and far weaker than if he had just eaten nothing.
cues.zh: 这也解释了为什么厄普顿·辛克莱说，水果或清淡的饮食刚好让他饿得发慌，而且比什么都不吃时虚弱得多。

cues.en: As I explained in my last video, insulin is necessary for glucose to get into the cell to be used for energy. When you eat carbohydrates,
cues.zh: 正如我在上个视频中所解释的，胰岛素是葡萄糖进入细胞转化为能量所必需的。当你吃碳水化合物时，

cues.en: the pancreas secretes insulin to deal with it and too much insulin hampers the action of something called hormone sensitive lipase
cues.zh: 胰腺会分泌胰岛素来处理它，而过多的胰岛素会阻碍一种叫做激素敏感性脂肪酶的物质发挥作用，

cues.en: which is necessary to mobilize fat and use it for fuel.
cues.zh: 这种物质对于动员脂肪并将其用作燃料是必不可少的。

cues.en: Though, keep in mind that grains or refined carbohydrates will produce a much higher insulin response than say green vegetables.
cues.zh: 不过请记住，谷物或精制碳水化合物产生的胰岛素反应要比绿叶蔬菜高得多。

cues.en: Now, because the body is having a hard time using its fat for fuel, it will do a couple things.
cues.zh: 现在，由于身体很难利用脂肪作为燃料，它会采取一些措施。

cues.en: One, it will simply slow down metabolism to preserve energy.
cues.zh: 第一，它会简单地减慢新陈代谢来保存能量。

cues.en: In the Minnesota Starvation Experiment, the subject's metabolism dropped by 40%.
cues.zh: 在明尼苏达饥饿实验中，受试者的新陈代谢下降了 40%。

cues.en: Their bodies didn't have access to its stored energy and their restricted calorie diets didn't provide much fuel, so there's no choice but to slow down the metabolism.
cues.zh: 它们身体无法利用储存的能量，而限制卡路里的饮食又提供不了多少燃料，所以别无选择，只能降低新陈代谢。

cues.en: Ironically, in the case of fasting, as Jason Fung points out, metabolism actually goes up. If you don't do anything about your insulin and just reduce your calories, your metabolism goes down. But what happens during fasting?
cues.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，正如杰森·芬格（Jason Fung）所指出，在禁食的情况下，新陈代谢实际上会上升。如果你对胰岛素置之不理，只是单纯减少卡路里，新陈代谢就会下降。但禁食期间会发生什么呢？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: here's a study of four consecutive days of fasting.
cues.zh: 这是一项关于连续四天禁食的研究。

cues.en: What happens to your REE?
cues.zh: 你的 REE 会发生什么变化？

cues.en: This is this middle line here. That's the resting energy expenditure.
cues.zh: 中间这条线就是。那是静息能量消耗。

cues.en: It doesn't go down.
cues.zh: 它没有下降。

cues.en: It goes up.
cues.zh: 反而上升了。

cues.en: You're burning more energy
cues.zh: 你消耗的能量变多了，

cues.en: than you did.
cues.zh: 比以前更多。

cues.en: The other thing that the body will do when it can't use fat for fuel is break down muscle into glucose through a process called gluconeogenesis.
cues.zh: 当身体无法利用脂肪作为燃料时，另一件会做的事是通过一种叫糖异生的过程把肌肉分解成葡萄糖。

cues.en: The body doesn't want to do this too much because it's not very smart to eat through something as important as muscle.
cues.zh: 身体其实不想做得太火候，因为把像肌肉这么重要的东西吃掉并不明智。

cues.en: But when it can't access its own stored energy, it's more likely to resort to this.
cues.zh: 但当它无法获取自身储存的能量时，就更有可能采取这种手段。

cues.en: This is why you'll experience more muscle loss on caloric restriction than if you ate nothing.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么你在热量限制下经历的肌肉流失，会比什么都不吃时还要多。

cues.en: When you are fasting, human growth hormone is released.
cues.zh: 当你禁食时，人体生长激素会被释放出来。

cues.en: As the name implies, human growth hormone is an anabolic hormone, a hormone conducive to growth.
cues.zh: 顾名思义，人体生长激素是一种合成代谢激素，也就是有利于生长的激素。

cues.en: In Leninger's principles of biochemistry textbook, they give the example of how injecting the human growth hormone gene into a mouse makes it unusually large.
cues.zh: 在莱宁格（Leninger）的《生物化学原理》教科书中，他们举了一个例子：将人体生长激素基因注射到老鼠体内，会使其变得异常巨大。

cues.en: As explained in Gaitan's textbook of medical physiology,
cues.zh: 正如盖顿医学生理学教科书中所解释的，

cues.en: growth hormone also mobilizes large quantities of free fatty acids from the adipose tissue and these in turn are used to supply most of the energy for the body cells,
cues.zh: 生长激素还会从脂肪组织中动员大量游离脂肪酸，这些脂肪酸进而为体细胞提供大部分能量，

cues.en: thus acting as a potent protein sparer.
cues.zh: 从而起到强效蛋白质节省剂的作用。

cues.en: That is human growth hormone is protecting your muscles from breaking down.
cues.zh: 也就是说，人体生长激素能保护你的肌肉不被分解。

cues.en: The study I referred to earlier about subjects undergoing an eighty four hour fast shows that growth hormone rises significantly
cues.zh: 我前面提到过的那项关于受试者进行84小时禁食的研究表明，生长激素会显著上升，

cues.en: after the second day of fasting.
cues.zh: 在禁食的第二天之后。

cues.en: As mentioned earlier, you should enter ketosis sometime within the first three days or so of fasting and it depends on how much you are moving around and what your diet was like before starting the fast.
cues.zh: 如前所述，你应该在禁食的前三天左右进入酮症状态，这取决于你的活动量以及开始禁食前的饮食情况。

cues.en: The state of ketosis is a great indicator that your body is making good use of its stored body fat for energy.
cues.zh: 酮症状态是一个很好的指标，表明你的身体正在充分利用储存的体脂来获取能量。

cues.en: In Tim Ferriss' book Tools of Titans,
cues.zh: 在蒂姆·费里斯的书《巨人的工具》中，

cues.en: Tim talks about his first clinically supervised seven day fast.
cues.zh: 蒂姆谈到了他第一次在临床监督下进行为期七天的禁食。

cues.en: For some sort of liability reasons, he wasn't allowed to exercise or leave the facility.
cues.zh: 出于某种责任险的原因，他不被允许锻炼或离开设施。

cues.en: Considering exercise is a potent stimulator of human growth hormone and will deplete glucose stores, not getting any exercise is a great way to prevent yourself from getting into ketosis during a fast.
cues.zh: 考虑到运动是人体生长激素的强效刺激剂，并会消耗葡萄糖储备，不进行任何运动是防止自己在禁食期间进入酮症状态的好方法。

cues.en: It's also a great way to lose muscle.
cues.zh: 这也是减掉肌肉的好方法。

cues.en: Tim says he lost 12 pounds of muscle during the overly restrictive clinically supervised seven day fast,
cues.zh: 蒂姆说，在那次过度限制、有临床监督的七天禁食期间，他减掉了12磅肌肉，

cues.en: but when following a protocol designed to get him into ketosis as soon as possible involving things like four hours of brisk walking, he did a ten day fast and apparently lost zero muscle mass.
cues.zh: 但当遵循一项旨在让他尽快进入酮症状态的方案（包含诸如四小时快走之类的事情）时，他进行了十天的禁食，显然肌肉量零流失。

cues.en: One last factor in ketosis preserving muscle is Leucine.
cues.zh: 生酮状态能保住肌肉，最后一个因素是亮氨酸。

cues.en: When you're in ketosis you have a higher fasting blood leucine level and leucine is a key branched chain amino acid that has an anabolic effect on the body so it preserves lean body mass.
cues.zh: 处于生酮状态时，你的空腹血亮氨酸水平更高；亮氨酸是一种关键的支链氨基酸，对身体有合成代谢作用，因此能保住瘦体重。

cues.en: A lot of people interested in building muscle may be worried that fasting or a ketogenic diet wouldn't work for them because insulin and therefore carbohydrates are necessary for protein synthesis I e muscle growth.
cues.zh: 很多想增肌的人可能担心，禁食或生酮饮食对他们没用，因为蛋白质合成——也就是肌肉增长——需要胰岛素，因此也需要碳水化合物。

cues.en: But actually this leucine fills that role and is a good trigger for protein synthesis.
cues.zh: 但实际上，亮氨酸正好承担了这个角色，能很好地触发蛋白质合成。

cues.en: So just to sum all this up, compared to a conventional calorie restricted diet, fasting means you lose more weight in the form of fat, you keep more muscle, you have more energy,
cues.zh: 所以总结一下：与常规的限制热量饮食相比，禁食意味着你减掉更多脂肪形式的体重，保留更多肌肉，也更有精力，

cues.en: and you're less hungry.
cues.zh: 而且没那么饿。

cues.en: If proper weight loss is your goal, it might be better to eat nothing at all rather than eating a conventional low calorie diet.
cues.zh: 如果目标是合理减重，那什么都不吃可能比吃常规低热量饮食更好。
